claims.text: The initial microstructure consists of dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Controlled solidification at 1400°C and a cooling rate of 10°C/min will optimize the lamellar colony architecture.
The controlled-solidification intervention will increase lamellar colony size.
The controlled-solidification intervention will reduce internal boundary density.
Increasing colony size and reducing internal boundary density will reduce microcrack initiation.
Increasing colony size and reducing internal boundary density will reduce microcrack propagation.
Reduced microcrack initiation and propagation will enhance damage tolerance.
Microstructural architecture influences deformation mechanisms and damage tolerance.
The intervention will increase room-temperature yield strength by 25%, from 800 MPa to 1000 MPa, relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The intervention will increase room-temperature tensile ductility by 35%, from 5% to 6.75%, relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The predicted improvements apply at 20–25°C and strain rates between 0.001 s^-1 and 0.01 s^-1.
